key_insight: The thesis shows that large action spaces can be made tractable by sharing statistical strength across actions, using structured Bayesian exploration on-policy and latent-variable or pessimistic objectives off-policy.
engineering_relevance: These methods are relevant for recommender systems, interactive decision-making, and other large-scale control problems where sparse feedback and many candidate actions make naive exploration or off-policy correction unstable.
method: meTS: mixed-effect Thompson sampling for on-policy learning with shared structure across actions.
dTS: diffusion-inspired priors that encode action dependencies and improve exploration efficiency.
sDM and pessimistic log-likelihood / PAC-Bayesian objectives for off-policy learning with better optimization and bias-variance control.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regret guarantees for the on-policy methods and theoretical/optimization results showing that optimization error can dominate estimation error in large-action off-policy learning.
watch_item: The proposed approaches rely on structured assumptions and efficient optimization; performance may degrade if the action relationships or logged-policy support are misspecified.
paper_title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
